minutes.headline: School Committee took up the next-year school operating budget, ratified a three-year teacher contract, and added two grade 9 choice slots.
minutes.summary: The superintendent presented the level-service school budget for next year. It covered enrollment, a seventh-grade foreign language cut, fewer paraprofessionals, health insurance, special education tuition and utility savings. The committee then moved on to the teacher contract agreement, two more school choice openings, a third reading of several policies and the outgoing chair's tribute. Most votes were taken by voice, and the captions do not carry the results.

public_comment.topic: A teacher spoke about the student food drive, the interest-based bargaining process and student community-service presentations.
A resident asked about the budget impact of the contract's longevity payments.

Accept two additional school choice openings in grade 9.
Approve the athletic advisory council, school lunch negative balance and facilities use policies on third reading.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented a level-service school operating budget for next year, and a motion on its bottom line followed; the result is not audible.
The committee took up the three-year teacher contract agreement with the educators association; a motion was made and seconded, and the result is not audible.
A motion to accept two additional school choice openings in grade 9 was made; the superintendent proposed using that choice money for the ski and lacrosse teams.
Health insurance renewed higher than budgeted, and one-time school choice funds that covered the gap last year must now be absorbed in the budget line.
Three policies went to a third reading and a Town Meeting auditorium food and drink waiver was moved; results for both are not audible.

why_it_matters: The school operating budget is the main school cost the town budget, mostly taxes, is asked to carry, and the contract, health insurance and special education tuition are among the lines that move it.
The state budget is not final, so circuit breaker and Chapter 70 aid could change what the district must cover from local sources.
Most votes were taken by voice and the captions do not carry the results, so the outcomes need to be checked against the official minutes.
